messages:
Kai Nguyen: Heads-up: thinking through warmup ordering for safetensors multi-shard models — want to capture edge cases before I write the follow-up RFC.
Kai Nguyen: Main questions: what the weights loader should promise vs what runtime should optimize for (ordering, parallel map vs stream, checksum timing).
Jess Patel: +1 that we need a clear interface. I'd prefer weightsource expose 'segments with hotness score' and let runtime decide ordering.
Mike Olson: Hotness score? how do we compute that cheaply? model metadata + recent seq length distribution?
Sara Li: We can approximate hotness by token-level access pattern: embeddings/kvcache segments first, then lm_head, then rest. For chat models kvcache blocks are highest priority.
Jess Patel: Also consider partial-shard mmap: mapping headers to inspect dtype/shape without touching entire file. That lets us schedule reads without full download.
Kai Nguyen: Agree. Proposal idea: weightsource API returns list of segment descriptors: [id, byte_range, role_tags (kvcache|params|embed|head), compressed?, checksum]. Runtime asks for warmable segments and issues async_map(segment_id) calls.
Zoe R.: One tricky case: tarball-overlay where shards are packed inside a .tar.gz blob (customer private deployment). We should support streaming extract so we can warm specific ranges without extracting whole archive.
Mike Olson: For tarballs we can expose virtual offsets in the manifest that map to underlying blob ranges. Implement streaming inflate with windowed reads and small inflate state for each segment.
Sara Li: Tradeoffs: eager checksum verification blocks startup if done synchronously. Suggest async checksum with optional integrity flag in manifest: runtime can choose to verify in background and mark segment 'verified' later.
Kai Nguyen: Good. Also need a fallback when mmap isn't supported (windows containers, CIFS mounts): memory-map-friendly loaders should fall back to staging read+pin to temp file. Keep same segment descriptor semantics.
Jess Patel: On ordering, simple heuristic that has worked in testing: 1) all kvcache segments, 2) first-n parameter shards needed for initial forward (e.g., embedding + first transformer block), 3) rest by size descending but capped to parallelism budget.
Kai Nguyen: I'd add a small code sketch for priority scoring we used:```python
def score_segment(seg, model_profile):
    score = 0
    if 'kvcache' in seg['role_tags']: score += 1000
    if 'embed' in seg['role_tags']: score += 500
    # prefer small chunks that unblock earlier
    score += max(0, 200 - seg['size_mb'])
    # boost if model profile indicates short sequences
    score += model_profile.get('short_seq_bias', 0)
    return score
```
Zoe R.: Also watch memory pressure. We should limit concurrent warm maps by a budget (bytes_in_flight). If budget exhausted, backpressure request acceptance at the RPC layer.
Mike Olson: Regarding sharded checkpoints and resumes: persist warm progress as a simple per-segment statefile with last_mapped_offset. On restart, we skip already-mapped ranges. Works with partial downloads.
Sara Li: Testing checklist: tarball overlay streams, mmap-disabled fallback, concurrent warm budget enforcement, async checksum race (start inference before verify). Also simulate network stalls so prefetch/backpressure logic is exercised.
Kai Nguyen: One more API boundary decision: weightsource SHOULD NOT decide global prefetch ordering beyond per-segment hotness; runtime keeps policy (latency vs cost). That keeps weightsource simple and portable.
Jess Patel: Agreed. Implementation note: add 'warmable_hint' field in manifest to allow manual tuning for problematic models.
deploy-bot: Deploy check: no infra changes required for this RFC follow-up draft.
Kai Nguyen: Thanks all — I'll draft the RFC follow-up with these points plus manifest example and a small test harness. Ping if you want to add more edge cases (NFS, HSM-protected blobs, encrypted shards). :thumbsup:
